title: Meta used AI to target workers with medical conditions for layoffs, lawsuit claims
source_used: DD News (wire-style report; original outlet not named in the text)
key_facts: Twenty-six Meta Platforms employees filed a lawsuit in federal court in Oakland, California, 'late Monday' (Monday before 9 Oct, so 5 Oct 2026 by inference).
They claim Meta used AI-powered software that disproportionately targeted people with disabilities or who took medical leave when choosing workers for layoffs.

The complaint says factors included productivity and AI token usage; systems named include 'Metamate', an LLM assistant, an employee-trained 'second brain', and a productivity score drawn from scanning keystrokes, screen content, emails and browser history.
Plaintiffs were told in May their jobs would end from 22 Jul; they seek a preliminary ruling blocking Meta from completing the layoffs while they pursue claims in private arbitration.
They cite federal and state anti-discrimination laws and say Meta failed to test its AI systems for bias, as recently adopted California and New York City laws require.
A spokesperson said workforce decisions 'were and are made by people, not AI'.
The report says the suit appears to be the first against a major US company over alleged use of AI in layoffs.
Meta cut 10% of its global workforce (nearly 8,000 people) in May.
quote_evidence: The lawsuit appears to be the first against a major U.S. company to challenge the alleged use of AI in conducting layoffs.
“Workforce management and organizational decisions were and are made by people, not AI,” the spokesperson said.
According to the complaint, Meta used a number of internal AI-assisted systems to score and rank employees on a termination list.
why_it_matters_hint: Tests whether AI-assisted ranking of staff for layoffs can break disability and anti-discrimination law.
event_date: Filed late Monday (5 Oct 2026 by inference)
notes: Allegations only; Meta's spokesperson denies AI made the decisions (the text says 'the spokesperson' without naming the company in the lines we have). The text looks like a wire report but names no wire; DD News is credited. The filing date is inferred from 'late Monday' and a 8 Oct Staffing Industry Analysts piece on AI layoff lawsuits.
